newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - First fixed rate for PCI Bank.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - First fixed rate for PCI Bank.

text.p: Asian debt markets offered a first fixed-rate bond for PCI Bank on Wednesday.
Philippine Commercial International Bank (PCI Bank) launched a US$100 million five-year Eurobond via lead manager Merrill Lynch.
The bonds will be priced to yield 120 to 130 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries. Fees are 50 basis points.
Pricing is expected by 1100 GMT on Thursday.

Hong Kong traders said the pricing on the PCI Bank deal is a bit tight, but noted the novelty value of the deal and anticipated strong support from dealers in PCI Bank's medium-term note programme will help make the deal a success.
Also, "even if the pricing is slightly on the high side, people will think that all Philippine issues are going to tighten anyway, so they will support the PCIB issue," said one dealer.
In other news of the Philippines, a U.S. Treasury seven-percent note was set as the benchmark for determining price and yields on the country's Brady bond exchange programme.
For the fixed-rate bond, the exchange yield was set at 9.25 percent, arranger J.P. Morgan Securities said.

From Thailand, Siam City Bank assistant vice president Ekapong Rugrien said Thai political uncertainty and an economic slowdown this year forced the bank to raise the premium on its US$115 million five-year bond issue to 100 basis points over U.S. Treasuries from a planned 85 basis points.
The bond was launched on Tuesday by lead manager J.P. Morgan Securities. With fees, the deal paid about 110 basis points to participants.
One Hong Kong banker said the pricing for the Siam City Bank issue was "spot on" given recent developments in the country.
"The pricing wasn't ultra-attractive, but it wasn't as tight as recent Thai issues such as Bangkok Bank," she said.
In other deals today, Hanil Bank, acting through its Hong Kong branch, set a HK$500 million 364-day floating rate certificate of deposit issue.
The certificates pay a margin of 30 basis points and an all-in of 38 basis points. Chase Manhattan Asia and Sakura Finance Asia are the arrangers.
